subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle/shutdown protocol now, or continue handling these races as targeted path-specific fixes until a narrower contract emerges?
rationale: Current main has localized cleanup and drain mechanisms, but the requested ResourceManager would define a cross-boundary runtime/plugin/session contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep design tracker and define protocol
options.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical design discussion and require a maintainer-owned API plan before any implementation PR.

options.title: Continue targeted fixes only
options.body: Close or de-scope the shared manager idea and rely on concrete symptom issues such as the missing-tool-result and session-lock reports.

options.title: Prototype behind one owner boundary
options.body: Allow a narrow experimental lifecycle helper in one owner area, but do not promote it to SDK/core until multiple paths prove the same invariant.

recommendation.title: Keep design tracker and define protocol
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical design discussion and require a maintainer-owned API plan before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the cross-runtime/plugin/session owner boundary, and prior review history already routes that broad lifecycle design surface to steipete.
